key_insight: HTP-Net improves dense welding stub counting by preserving fine boundaries and topology while separating heavily overlapping slender instances.
engineering_relevance: The method enables more reliable warehouse inventory and morphological measurement of welding electrodes and wire stubs in factory vision systems.
method: Wavelet-Driven Edge-Preserving module keeps subtle boundaries during downsampling.
Long-Range Topology Representation Block models global context to avoid broken slender masks.
Orientation-Driven Instance Segmentation Head uses rotation-aware priors to reduce NMS conflicts and mask overlap.
evidence_signal: On custom and public dense-slender-target datasets, the model improves mAP50 by at least 1.2% and up to 55.3%, and the deployed system reports 99% accuracy for electrodes and 94% for wire stubs in factory testing.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may still depend on consistent imaging conditions and calibration, since dense overlap and boundary ambiguity remain challenging in industrial scenes.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
